chunks: 'Alam al-Huda Muhammad ibn al-Fayd al-Kashani states in Nadd al-Idah (p. 315), after mentioning his complete lineage going back to Ya'rub ibn Qahtan, he said:

(Abu Abdillah, known as Ibn al-Mu'allim — the chief of the mutakallimun of the Imamiyya and their fuqaha'; the scholarly leadership of their community ended with him in his era in knowledge and jurisprudence (fiqh). He has close to two hundred works.)

key_terms.الْإِمَامِيَّةِ: the Imamiyya — the Twelver Shia community
key_terms.نَضْدِ: arrangement/compilation (part of the book title Nadd al-Idah)

ai.seo_question: Who was Abu Abdillah Ibn al-Mu'allim and what was his standing among the scholars of the Imamiyya?
ai.summary: This passage from the chapter of praises in Tahdhib al-Ahkam cites 'Alam al-Huda Muhammad ibn al-Fayd al-Kashani's Nadd al-Idah, which traces the lineage of Abu Abdillah (Sheikh al-Mufid) back to the legendary Arab ancestor Ya'rub ibn Qahtan and extols him as the supreme leader of the Imami theologians and jurists of his era. His nearly two hundred written works serve as testimony to an unmatched scholarly authority recognized by later generations.
